core_obligations: Deduce the two conditions from the earlier statements on coverings by thickenings and factorisation through a stage (proof lines 2108-2110).

For the converse, form the category of representable thickenings from affine schemes into the sheaf, and show it is directed: it is non-empty, the coproduct of two objects factors through a third, and there is at most one arrow between any two objects (proof lines 2112-2120).
Write the sheaf as the colimit over that category, which by the hypothesis is a filtered colimit of affine schemes (proof lines 2120-2122).

Show that the arrows of the category are thickenings, so that the colimit is the required presentation, by identifying an arrow with the projection of a fibre product and using that the target is a monomorphism (proof lines 2122-2126).
proof_roadmap: Easy direction from earlier statements (proof lines 2108-2110).
Directedness of the category of thickenings (proof lines 2112-2120).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises a sheaf on the fppf site being an affine formal algebraic space by two conditions: that every morphism from an affine scheme factors through a representable thickening from an affine scheme, and a set-theoretic condition recalled from a remark (statement lines 2095-2106). One direction follows from two earlier statements of the chapter. For the converse the proof builds the presentation explicitly: the category of representable thickenings from affine schemes is shown to be directed, which uses that the coproduct of two such thickenings can be factored through a third and that between any two objects there is at most one arrow, and the sheaf is written as the colimit over that category, which by hypothesis is a filtered colimit of affine schemes (proof lines 2108-2122). It remains to see that the transition arrows in that presentation are thickenings, which is proved by writing a thickening as a fibre product with itself over the target and using that the target is a monomorphism of sheaves (proof lines 2122-2126). The claim is H2: the two properties defining the presentation -- directedness of the index category and the fact that its arrows are thickenings -- are each verified, the second by a short fibre product computation.
